One of the descendants of Trinh Phuc Loi, Trinh Van Bo, operated his business at number 48 on Hang Ngang Street. In addition to silk and textile shops, Hang Ngang Street was also known for its tea shops run by Chinese immigrants.

On August 19, 1945, after the successful uprising against the colonial regime in Hanoi, Truong Chinh and other members of the Central Committee met at number 48 to discuss further actions and preparations for Ho Chi Minh's return to the city. Ho Chi Minh arrived in Hanoi on August 24, staying briefly in Phu Xa and then moving to Phu Gia, both now part of Phu Thuong commune in Tu Liem district.

On August 25, he returned to the city center and stayed at number 48, the residence of Trinh Van Bo and his wife, Hoang Minh Ho, who were active members of the Viet Minh. Here, Ho Chi Minh chaired the first meeting of the Central Committee in Hanoi, deciding on key issues such as organizing a mass rally to introduce the new government and drafting the Declaration of Independence, a document of immense importance in Vietnam's history of nation-building and defense.
